harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built dual-transit redundant routing between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) carrying traffic between node3's and node4's private subnets, with automatic failover verified across a live transit-network outage, then confirmed persistence via individual reboots of all four nodes.
actions_performed: Discovered topology via targeted addressing/ping probes: node1(VyOS eth1/eth2)<->node2(OPNsense vtnet1/vtnet2) are the two transit networks; node1 eth3<->node3 eth1 and node2 vtnet3<->node4 eth1 are the private links
Root-caused a dead end: 169.254.0.0/16 (link-local) addressing was silently non-forwardable on FreeBSD/OPNsense per RFC3927; renumbered all segments to 10.201.1-4.0/24

Configured VyOS (node1) with floating static routes to node4's subnet via both transit next-hops (distance 1 vs 10, pinned to specific interfaces to avoid recursive-via-default-route false positives) plus a default-deny forward firewall with explicit accepts

Configured OPNsense (node2) via config.xml surgery: opt1/opt2/opt3 interfaces, GW_T1/GW_T2 gateway objects with dpinger monitoring, a gateway group, firewall pass rules, and (after discovering OPNsense static routes cannot target gateway groups) a small root-privileged failover-monitor script registered as a configd action plus a persistent cron job keeping the static route to node3's subnet pointed at whichever transit gateway is reachable
Configured node3 and node4 (RHEL7) with static addressing and routes via persistent nmcli connection profiles
Verified healthy baseline connectivity node3<->node4 via transit1

Disrupted transit1 (admin-down on both node1 eth1 and node2 vtnet1) while running a continuous background ping from node3; confirmed both routers converged onto transit2 with only ~1.2s of packet loss during the live transition, then restored transit1 and confirmed both routers reconverged back automatically
Fixed a latent nmcli autoconnect=no bug on node3/node4 connection profiles discovered during the reboot test

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: rebooted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time, captured boot-identity change (boot_id/kern.boottime) for each, and verified full config/routing/firewall/gateway-monitor/cron persistence and end-to-end node3<->node4 connectivity after each reboot

evidence.requirement: Redundant routing carries traffic between node3 and node4 private networks across both transit paths
evidence.summary: node3->node4 ping succeeds 5/5 once VyOS floating static route and OPNsense static route+dpinger gateways were in place

evidence.requirement: Connectivity continues when transit network 1 is taken out of service, demonstrated across the transition
evidence.summary: eth1 disabled on node1 and vtnet1 downed on node2; both routers converged onto transit2 (confirmed via VyOS RIB and OPNsense routing table); node3's continuous background ping log showed only 4 lost packets (~1.2s) across the entire outage-and-restore cycle, then normal operation resumed on transit1

evidence.requirement: Transit1 restoration and reconvergence back to primary path
evidence.summary: eth1/vtnet1 re-enabled; VyOS route and OPNsense static route both automatically reverted to the transit1 gateway; final ping showed 0% loss
boot_id changed from ebd78841... to e325be07...; interfaces, static routes, forwarding and firewall rules all persisted

kern.boottime changed from 05:46:13 to 06:18:35; interfaces, static route, dpinger gateway monitors, firewall pass rules, and the failover cron job all persisted; node3<->node4 connectivity fully recovered
boot_id changed from 79b6a980... to 51111b32... (second reboot, after fixing a discovered nmcli autoconnect bug); eth1 addressing and route came up automatically and node4 was reachable
boot_id changed from b35fad86... to 5bd23b31...; eth1 addressing and route came up automatically and final end-to-end ping from node3 succeeded 5/5
